brief.ask: Create a brand identity for Dozeline, the iOS and Android wind-down and sleep journal app in this folder.
brief.owner: Owner preferences: calm, warm, not clinical, no moons or stars cliché. The app icon must be recognisable on a home screen at small sizes. English and Turkish markets.

claim.notes: Only settle passed the critic gate (blind 6/6/7, average 6.2, a narrow pass); descend and lamplit were rejected, and finalize needed --accept-risk because originality is insufficient-evidence (no trademark registry searches done).

concepts.title: Stepping Down
readsAs: a declining line chart / drop-off graph
a stair-rail or bent pipe. Unfortunate: a falling chart ('your sleep is crashing') or a worm in a bedtime app
concepts.sketchNotes: Reads as: s1 a tilde / swung dash, a generic stroke with nothing to own (struck); s2 a playground slide or ski jump, i.e. the swoosh family, the swell does not read as falling asleep (struck); s4 a boot, sock or hockey stick, an unfortunate and comic first reading (struck); s3 a line settling down in two decelerating steps, which is the closest any of them comes to its idea, and it has the lowest stock-shape similarity (0.19). Keep: one continuous even stroke, warm terracotta, a long flat rest at the end. Risks to fix: (1) at 16 px it collapses into a squiggle or tilde, so the second dip must be clearly shallower and the final flat at least as long as the whole descent, so the slowing is visible small; (2) don't let the two bumps go equal or it becomes a staircase or a wave/water icon; (3) the high start must not hook or curl, or it turns into a slide or a cane; (4) give it one ownable detail (terminal shape, stroke weight relation, or a frame/ground) so it is not just a line anyone could draw. Weak survivor: development must earn distinctiveness.

concepts.title: One Light On
readsAs: a small house or cabin with a sloped roof and a tall rounded door
the digit 0 (or letter O) set in a pentagon tag
a generic home/door UI icon, or a price tag. Unfortunate: a big zero, i.e. a score of 0, for an app whose promise is no scores
concepts.sketchNotes: Reads as: s1 a boho rainbow / tunnel (cliche, nested arches); s2 a gravestone or mouse-hole with a dot, webcam/record button (gravestone is the worst possible misreading for a sleep app, struck); s3 an arched window at night with one pane lit; s4 a bullseye/target or setting sun (sun-sets-for-sleep cliche, struck). s3 is the strongest idea on all three boards: one light left on in a dark house is warm, domestic, not moon/star, and reads at 16 px. Risks to fix: the symmetric 2x2 grid flirts with the Windows logo and generic 'home/window' icons - break symmetry (one off-centre mullion, or just two panes with the lit one low), let the lit pane glow (soft warm inner light, not a flat beige square), and keep the dark panes warm brown not black so it never turns into a tombstone. Make the arch proportion tall and slim like a real bedroom window.

concepts.title: Settled D
readsAs: a soft slumped pebble or creature with one closed eye
a mouse-hole or slot in a soft blob
a capital D sagging onto its back. Unfortunate: a piggy-bank coin slot or a toaster
concepts.sketchNotes: Reads as: s1 a fat rounded D with a small low hole (generic letter in a rounded font); s2 an E / list icon made of bars (initial built from slices, struck); s3 an E or Pac-Man/eye, slot cut into the D (initial with a cut, struck; Headspace review risk); s4 a plain rounded-sans D, open at top-left, reads as a font letter; s5 a nested D-in-D (nested copy, struck). s1 is the only one whose idea (weight settled to the bottom) is visible at all, via the sunk counter, but today it is a stock D (stock 0.81, Headspace-adjacent blob). Must change: exaggerate the slump so it reads as a resting pebble/body first and a D second - lower, wider, shoulder visibly sagging right, asymmetric organic contour, counter a soft horizontal pill hugging the base. Warm the colour off the mauve-brown. Risk: if it still reads 'D in a rounded font' after development, kill it.
